A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same tutoring-RL study. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original tutor-training experiments, simulated student outcomes on BigMath, benchmark evaluations, ablations, and example conversations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports revised descriptive counts, an additional table entry, and a replacement conversation example.

M1.justification: The GRPO procedure, student–tutor environment, correctness and pedagogical rewards, hard-reward variant, thinking tags, and auxiliary template rewards are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BigMath sources, MathTutorBench tasks, and MMLU, GSM8K, and MATH500 evaluations. The replacement illustrative problem remains within the existing math-tutoring coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main, reasoning, and MathTutorBench tables, including SFT, MDPO, SocraticLM, LearnLM, and general-purpose LLM baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the 10,000/500 training/test split, filtering criteria, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets. The λ=0.25 setting was already plotted in v1 Figure 3. Revised histogram counts do not document a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The positive tutoring case in v1 Figure 11 is replaced by v2 Figure 5: a calculator dialogue giving an incorrect answer becomes a flower-pot dialogue reaching the correct answer through guidance. The other cases and quantitative ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Sampling and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-training-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds the λ=0.25 row: 29.3% Δsolve rate, 32.0% leakage, and 2.3/1.8 Ped-RM micro/macro; this setting was already partially reported graphically. Histogram counts change from a total of 11,945 to 10,500, including 4,352 to 3,828 in the hardest bucket. One dialogue is replaced; matched aggregate benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The dialog/MDP formulation, reward equations, and auxiliary reward definitions are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims remain synthetic-data training without human annotations, control of the pedagogy–accuracy trade-off, competitive small-model tutoring, and preservation of reasoning capabilities.

C2.justification: The interpretations of leakage, student success, reasoning preservation, and thinking tags remain substantively unchanged. The limitations concerning synthetic students, math-only tutoring, delayed learning assessment, and absent human validation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 Section 5.2 explicitly identifies the previously reported 25%/66% accuracies as pre-dialog training-set solve rates; v1 Appendix B described them more generally as dataset accuracies. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, quantization, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.1 adds an explicit contrast with Daheim et al. (2024), emphasizing that the model learns planning during training. This is a limited positioning refinement. Bibliographic updates otherwise refer to the same cited works.

P1.justification: Dataset details move from Appendix B into Section 5.2. Other edits include a reasoning-benchmark label, local wording and caption corrections, a rewritten thinking-tag explanation, and updated affiliation and acknowledgement text.

P2.justification: The dataset histogram and composition table move into the main text, conversation figures precede the prompt figures, and the main results table gains a row. The positive-example figure is replaced, while the overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: The histogram now totals 10,500, agreeing with the stated split, and the positive tutoring illustration reaches a correct answer instead of presenting the incorrect calculator answer of 81 as successful tutoring. Replacing that example loses the same-problem contrast with DeepSeek, but improves the illustration's validity. These corrections and clearer reporting provide modest gains while the method and aggregate findings remain unchanged.
